key_insight: An automated CMR pipeline using local LLMs and fine-tuned vision foundation models can reliably extract labels, process images, and classify major cardiomyopathies with strong diagnostic performance.
clinical_relevance: If validated in practice, this approach could support faster, more standardized CMR interpretation and reduce dependence on manual report curation.
method: Used open-source, locally run LLMs to extract diagnostic labels from narrative CMR reports.
Preprocessed multimodal CMR data, including cine and late-gadolinium-enhancement (LGE) sequences.
Fine-tuned three vision foundation models (DINO, VST, UMedPT) and combined them in ensemble strategies.
evidence_signal: In an independent test set of 1,067 patients, ensemble models achieved high AUCs, including 0.959 for HCM and 0.966 for cardiac amyloidosis.
watch_item: Performance was evaluated on curated retrospective data, so generalizability across sites, scanners, and real-world workflows still needs prospective validation.
paper_title: Development of an automated, reliable, and clinically meaningful artificial intelligence (AI) tool for diagnosing cardiac disease from conventional cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) images
